amortization_base.engine_limitation_note: ENGINE LIMITATION -- READ BEFORE RELYING ON THE GENERATED SCHEDULE'S scheduled_principal FIGURES. The agreement's own wording ('0.60% of BEGINNING funded debt') and the borrower's own certified monthly Debt & Covenant tabs (04 Reporting/Period Archive/<YYYY>/<MM>/a.xlsx, 'Debt & Covenant' sheet) both confirm this is a DECLINING-BALANCE (self-amortizing) mechanic, not a flat percentage of original principal: verified exactly across 8 non-adjacent months (2025-01 through 2025-06, 2025-12, 2026-01, 2026-06) that 'Repayments' = 0.006 x that month's own 'Beginning Debt' to the cent -- e.g. $392,164.34 in 2025-01 (0.006 x $65,360,723.38) declining to $354,027.20 by 2026-06 (0.006 x $59,004,534.00). debt_service.py v1's amortization_base concept instead computes the base as 'the aggregate original principal of all fundings dated strictly before the payment date' -- for this single up-front-funded tranche that base is FIXED at $65,360,723.38 for the life of the loan (no further draws), so the engine computes a FLAT $392,164.34 installment every month instead of the true shrinking one. The generated schedule below therefore ties the certified figure in month 1 only; from month 2 onward the engine's cumulative scheduled principal is progressively HIGHER than the certified declining-balance paydown, and the gap widens every month (by 2026-06 -- 17 months of amortization -- the flat schedule would have paid down roughly $6.67M vs. the certified ~$6.36M actually paid, a gap that keeps compounding through the 60-month term). This is an engine capability gap (no declining-balance amortization base supported in v1), not a data-entry error -- flagged as a step-7 ambiguity with the two paths forward (accept the flat approximation and reconcile scheduled_principal to the certificates by hand each period, or hold the covenant-support 'scheduled_principal' row and have build-monitoring-model read the certified Debt & Covenant tab directly instead).

ambiguities: The Credit Agreement states NO day-count convention at all -- unlike a typical facility's 'actual days elapsed over a 360-day year' language, INTEREST AND FEES (p.4) says only 'Interest accrues at SOFR plus 6.25%, subject to a 2.00% SOFR floor. Interest is payable monthly in arrears.' actual/360 with both endpoints counted is recorded here as an ASSUMPTION (the market-standard convention for a SOFR facility, and debt_service.py's supported default), not a stated term. MATERIAL FINDING, larger than the usual stub-day ambiguity: the borrower's own certified monthly Debt & Covenant figures do NOT use any actual-day-count convention at all -- Cash Interest / Beginning Debt is IDENTICAL to 10 significant digits (0.906605097613...%) in every month checked (2025-01 through 2025-06), regardless of whether the month has 28, 30 or 31 days, which is only possible if the certified figures apply a flat (index+margin)/12 monthly-equivalent rate rather than any actual/360 or actual/365 calculation. No single pinned index rate can make this engine's actual/360 accrual reproduce the certified dollar amounts across months of different lengths. This means the generated schedule's cash-interest figures will NOT tie to the certified schedule even in ordinary, non-stub months -- a materially larger and more persistent gap than the funding/maturity-stub question this field is normally used to flag. Step-7 question: should the generated (actual/360) schedule stand as the CONTRACTUAL read notwithstanding the mismatch, or should the certified Debt & Covenant tab's flat-monthly convention be treated as the operative one (the engine has no 30/360-flat-monthly mode, so that would mean sourcing the cash-interest covenant-support figures from the certificate directly rather than from this generated schedule)?

_fees_not_modeled_note: The executed Fee Letter (7.pdf) states four ONE-TIME closing fees, all 'earned and payable on the closing date' and 'paid from sponsor equity ... [that] do not increase funded debt': Origination fee $1,960,821.70; Structuring fee $650,000.00; Documentation and diligence fee $239,178.30; Agency setup fee $150,000.00; Total $3,000,000.00. Confirmed against the Closing Funding Request (6.pdf), which funds only the $65,360,723.38 legacy-debt payoff with no fee draw -- consistent with the fees being paid outside the loan proceeds. No annual, recurring, monitoring, or exit fee is stated anywhere in the Fee Letter or Credit Agreement (full-text sweep for 'annual fee', 'administration fee', 'monitoring fee', 'exit fee', 'prepayment premium', 'make-whole' returns no hits). None of the three fees.when enum values ('close_and_payment_dates', 'payment_dates', 'maturity') represents a ONE-TIME, close-only cadence: 'close_and_payment_dates' would incorrectly repeat the $3,000,000 at every one of the 60 monthly payment dates through maturity; 'payment_dates' would repeat it 60 times with no closing occurrence; 'maturity' would misplace it five years late. Rather than generate a fee schedule that is silently and dramatically wrong (the same limitation documented in Nemeris's debt-service-spec.json for its closing/admin fees), the $3,000,000 in closing fees is OMITTED from the modeled fees[] array and flagged here for the analyst / engine owner. None of these fees would be a covenant Fixed Charge in any case -- this facility carries no Fixed Charges / coverage covenant at all (see covenant-spec.json) -- and none increases funded debt.

index_rates.source: ASSUMPTION derived from the certified January 2025 Debt & Covenant tab (04 Reporting/Period Archive/2025/01/a.xlsx): Cash Interest $592,563.65 / Beginning Debt $65,360,723.38 = 0.9066051% for the month; back-solved assuming that figure is a flat (index+margin)/12 monthly-equivalent rate (see day_count.ambiguities) gives an implied SOFR of approximately 4.6293% (0.9066051% x 12 = 10.8792611...%, less the 6.25% margin). No SOFR rate notice or published index print appears anywhere in the executed documents or the deal folder; this is the closest available data point, and it is itself convention-dependent -- see day_count.ambiguities for why no single actual/360 or actual/365 rate can reproduce the certified figures across months of different lengths. Held flat for the life of the generated schedule per the engine's standard (disclosed) behavior.

_covenant_support_rows_note: This agreement's only financial covenant (Maximum Total Leverage Ratio, covenant-spec.json id 'max_total_leverage') is a leverage test, not a Fixed-Charges/coverage test, so no covenant-spec definition currently binds to these two row labels. Captured anyway per Method step 3b so build-monitoring-model can populate a real cash-interest and scheduled-principal view in the model, distinct from the native Income Statement 'Interest Expense' row (which nets in $50,000/month of Deferred Financing Fee Amortization on top of Cash Interest per borrower-config.json model_lines._gap_note, and is therefore NOT the same figure as the facility's own contractual cash interest). If a future amendment adds an FCCR/DSCR covenant, its Fixed_Charges definition should bind to exactly these two labels. Given the amortization_base and day_count engine-limitation findings above, neither row's generated figures should be assumed to tie to the borrower's certified Debt & Covenant tab -- see those notes for the expected direction and growing magnitude of the drift.
